trust_boundaries: on-prem-to-cloud: dc01 and aad_connect/hybrid_agent to entra_id (hybrid sync)
adcs-internal: enrollment_svc to issuing_ca to root_ca (certificate chain)
architecture_summary.operational_context: Hybrid on-prem Active Directory with Azure AD Connect sync to Entra ID; AD Certificate Services for PKI

threat_actors.name: Network-Adjacent Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Domain compromise via AD certificate services misconfiguration (ESC attacks)
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Initial access to ws01 via phishing or vulnerability exploitation, then AD CS enumeration
non_capabilities: No physical access to DC or CA hardware
No ability to modify root CA directly without CA admin privileges

threat_actors.name: Compromised Domain User
threat_actors.motivation: Privilege escalation to domain admin via AD CS certificate template abuse
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Valid low-privilege domain credentials — either stolen or via initial phishing
non_capabilities: No high-privilege AD permissions at start
No direct DC network access blocked by tier model (if implemented)
No NTDS direct read access without DC sync privileges

attack_paths.entry_point: Spearphishing email with malicious attachment targeting domain user
attack_paths.impact: Initial foothold on domain-joined workstation with user-level domain credentials
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Phishing is primary initial access vector in enterprise environments; domain-joined workstations are high-value targets

attack_paths.entry_point: ESC1 — misconfigured certificate template allowing arbitrary SAN enrollment by low-priv user
attack_paths.impact: Certificate issued with Domain Admin SAN, enabling domain admin impersonation via PKINIT
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: ESC1 is the most common AD CS misconfiguration; certipy/Certify automate discovery and exploitation

attack_paths.entry_point: Golden ticket creation after obtaining krbtgt hash from NTDS via AP-004
attack_paths.impact: Persistent domain admin access via forged Kerberos tickets; survives password reset of individual accounts
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires NTDS access (AP-004); krbtgt hash enables unlimited persistence

attack_paths.entry_point: DCSync via domain admin privileges obtained from AP-002
attack_paths.impact: All domain credential hashes exfiltrated — full domain compromise
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: DCSync is standard post-exploitation after DA; NTDS dump enables offline cracking of all accounts

attack_paths.entry_point: AAD Connect compromise — attacker with domain admin adds malicious sync rules
attack_paths.impact: Entra ID accounts compromised via hybrid sync manipulation; cloud identity poisoned from on-prem foothold
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: AAD Connect runs as privileged service; DA access enables cloud identity poisoning through sync manipulation

attack_paths.entry_point: Modify Group Policy to disable endpoint defenses after domain admin compromise
attack_paths.impact: Endpoint security disabled across all domain-joined machines; lateral movement at scale
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: GPO modification is standard post-DA activity; disabling AV/EDR removes detection capability

attack_paths.entry_point: Credentials cached in admin workstation memory or scripts
attack_paths.impact: Domain admin credentials harvested without requiring ADCS exploitation
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Admin workstations frequently have cached credentials; mimikatz-class tools extract from LSASS

attack_paths.entry_point: CA admin compromise enabling installation of rogue certificate into trusted root store
attack_paths.impact: Attacker-controlled CA trusted by all domain systems; enables MitM of all TLS within domain
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires CA admin privileges (higher than DA in most orgs); extreme impact if achieved

mitigations.control_name: Security awareness training and phishing simulation
AD CS template hardening — remove CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT on sensitive templates
Privileged Access Workstations and tier model enforcement
AAD Connect least privilege and MFA for sync account
GPO change monitoring and SIEM alerting on policy modification
Credential Guard and LSASS protection on admin workstations
Root CA offline storage and CA admin role separation

findings.severity_rationale: ESC1 misconfiguration allows any domain user to obtain a DA certificate; entire domain is compromised in one step
NTDS dump via DCSync provides all domain credentials; recovery requires full domain rebuild if krbtgt reset not done
Cloud identity poisoning via AAD Connect extends on-prem compromise to Entra ID; cross-boundary blast radius
Admin workstation credential exposure is likely lateral movement enabler; Credential Guard partially deployed
Golden ticket persistence requires krbtgt hash (AP-004 prerequisite); impact is severe but attack chain is multi-step
GPO modification detection is implemented; residual risk is attacker speed vs detection lag
Root CA offline and CA admin separated; rogue CA installation would require compromise of both offline CA and admin separation
Phishing is primary initial access; training is implemented but residual click rate persists
